documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence General Use Guidelines
documents.summary: UW-IT general-use guidelines for generative AI, mostly about data privacy, approved tools, and user responsibility. A short acceptable-use section hands the course-level rule to instructors and tells students to follow it.
documents.stance_why: Coder A coded delegates, coder B permit. The page opens 'The University supports the responsible use of generative AI (GenAI) when helpful to further its mission' and sets conditions on use (approved services for University data, review of output, disclosure, records), so the document takes a stance itself: permit with conditions. Only one short passage ('Course instructors have the discretion to allow, prohibit, or put parameters around the use of GenAI') hands course rules to instructors, so delegates does not describe the whole document.

units.why: The opening sentence states the university's overall position that it 'supports the responsible use of generative AI', a framework statement of purpose and principle, so P56 with a permit stance addressed to everyone.
units.anchor: The University supports the responsible use of generative AI (GenAI) when helpful to further its

units.why: Says the guidelines are 'general advice for the UW community', not binding rules; this states what the document is and covers, so it is a scope statement (P61), not a framework principle.
units.anchor: These guidelines provide general advice for the UW community
units.fit_note: Coder A coded this as P56 framework preamble; the sentence states the guidelines' non-binding scope rather than a principle.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The sentence is a real statement of the guidelines' scope ('general advice', not rules), so it is kept. Coder A's P56 is replaced by P61 because P56 is already used for the opening sentence on support for responsible use and this sentence only scopes the document.

units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: during-work, B: general). Final: phase general. The sentence limits University data to approved services in general, not at a particular point in coursework, so phase is general (coder B), not during-work.

units.why: Warns that unapproved tools and unauthorized data release 'could result in violations of policy or law', a consequence tied to compliance with policy and law, P77.

units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The warning ('could result in violations of policy or law for which you or the University may be liable') is a real statement of consequence for unapproved use, so it is kept as a compliance statement, P77, informs.

units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A: restrict, B: neutral). Final: unit_stance neutral. 'All use of GenAI must comply with all relevant UW policies and standards' sets a compliance duty and takes no position on whether AI is used, so unit_stance is neutral.

units.why: The sentence offers 'complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments', an institutional offer of AI training; P70 fits best since it is not faculty-only.
units.anchor: Complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments are available

units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance (A: encourage, B: neutral). Final: unit_stance neutral. Offering training and tool review is an institutional service and does not welcome or require AI use itself, so neutral rather than encourage.

documents.summary: Teaching@UW page of sample syllabus and assignment statements that instructors adapt, with advice on drafting a policy. It states that there is no single UW-wide AI policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'there is no single university-wide UW AI policy' and offers samples for 'conditional use' and 'prohibiting any AI use', so the stance is left to each instructor, with tiers listed.

units.why: States the page's purpose: 'examples you can adapt to articulate your expectations for whether and how students may use AI'. Leaves the choice to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: examples you can adapt to articulate your expectations for whether and how students may use
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The sentence ('examples you can adapt to articulate your expectations for whether and how students may use AI') states the page's purpose: instructors decide whether and how students may use AI. It is a real statement of who decides, so it is kept as P04.

units.why: The page says stating expectations in 'both the syllabus and assignment instructions' helps students avoid unauthorized use, advising instructors to state AI expectations in both places, P09.
units.anchor: Stating your expectations in both the syllabus and assignment instructions helps students avoid unauthorized use

units.why: 'there is no single university-wide UW AI policy' states that the rule is left to courses, matching P04 (instructor-level decision).

units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A: course-start, B: general); modality (A: should, B: informs); policy_type (A: P11, B: P04). Final: phase general, modality informs, policy_type P04. Coder B's normalized policy only restated the anchor, so the anchor alone is used (policy null). The passage has two statements: a fact (no single university-wide policy) and a recommendation to discuss expectations in the syllabus and on the first day. The fact is coded here as P04 (the decision falls to courses); P11 (coder A) is not used because the sentence does not say a course policy governs only that course. The recommendation is a separate unit (P66). A's fit note is kept.

units.why: Discussing expectations 'on the first day of class' goes beyond posting the rule to talking about it, and clarifies differences across courses; P66 fits better than P09 because it is about discussion, not the syllabus statement.
units.anchor: discussing your expectations in the syllabus and on the first day of class
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. Coder A noted this recommendation only in a fit_note and did not code it. The sentence recommends 'discussing your expectations in the syllabus and on the first day of class' to promote integrity, an instruction distinct from the fact in the same sentence, so it is kept as its own unit. P66 (discuss the rules with students) fits better than P09 (syllabus statement).
